sections.h2: Where is Wilsonville, Oregon, and why does it sit in two counties?
sections.html:
Wilsonville is a Clackamas County city on the south edge of the Portland metro area, with its northern section in Washington County. It lies on the north side of the Willamette River, and Interstate 5 runs through it and crosses the river on the Boone Bridge.

The city covers about 7.5 square miles of land by the Census Bureau’s count. Tualatin lies to the north, Sherwood to the northwest, and Canby and Aurora to the southeast. Charbonneau, a planned community inside city limits, sits south of the river.

The county split affects sellers directly. Most parcels are billed and recorded in Clackamas County, but a house in the Washington County section follows that county’s tax dates and recording rules.

sections.h2: What is the history of Wilsonville?
sections.html:
Wilsonville began as a river ferry landing. Alphonso Boone, a grandson of Daniel Boone, founded Boones Landing in 1846, and his ferry across the Willamette opened in 1847. The area moved from Yamhill County to Clackamas County in 1855, and the town was renamed Wilsonville on June 3, 1880, after first postmaster Charles Wilson.

The railroad arrived by 1890. The Boone Bridge opened in 1954 and the ferry was retired. Wilsonville incorporated on October 10, 1968, with about 1,000 residents, and Charbonneau was annexed in 1971. Census counts then rose from 1,001 in 1970 to 7,106 in 1990, 13,991 in 2000, 19,509 in 2010 and 26,664 in 2020.

Two later projects changed the map. Dammasch State Hospital operated from 1961 until it closed in 1995, and its site became the Villebois neighborhood. Coffee Creek Correctional Facility opened in 2001. Most of the housing here is therefore newer than in older Portland suburbs, which affects both repair needs and buyer expectations.

sections.h2: What do Census Bureau figures show for Wilsonville?
sections.html:
Wilsonville stands out because renters outnumber owners. The Census Bureau’s 2020 to 2024 estimates give this picture.

With 49.0% owner-occupied housing, a good share of the city’s single-family houses, townhomes and condos are rentals. A seller whose tenant has moved out, or who owns a rental with deferred upkeep, is a common Wilsonville scenario.

sections.h2: Which employers keep Wilsonville busy on weekdays?
sections.html:
Wilsonville has a large employment base for a city of its size. The city’s 2024 financial report lists the top employers:

EmployerEmployeesShare of jobs
Siemens Mentor Graphics1,0145.9%
Coca-Cola Bottling6133.6%
Collins Aerospace5273.1%
Sysco Food Services4992.9%

The ten largest employers together account for 4,457 jobs, or 26.1%. The city describes a considerable weekday workforce of manufacturers, distributors, high-tech firms and retailers. Oregon Institute of Technology and a Clackamas Community College branch have campuses here. That daytime workforce is one reason rentals and townhomes near the east side do well, and it gives sellers a pool of local buyers and tenants.

Wilsonville is divided into several distinct residential areas, each with its own housing mix. The city’s economic development page describes them.

  • Villebois. The largest new neighborhood on the west side, modeled on a European village with homes, condos, row homes, apartments and a small commercial district.
  • Charbonneau. A golf course community started in 1972, with about 3,500 residents. Its students attend Canby School District schools.
  • Old Town and the west side. Near Boones Ferry Park, with neighborhoods such as The Park at Merryfield, Montebello and Fox Chase.
  • East side. Home to Wilsonville High School, Memorial Park, the library and city offices, with neighborhoods including Canyon Creek Estates, Wilsonville Meadows and Landover.
  • Frog Pond. Master-planned land on the northeast edge, with homes under construction.

Frog Pond planning covers about 500 acres, with roughly 220 inside the urban growth boundary. The school district owns land there for a future middle school, a primary school and sports fields. Frog Pond’s new construction competes with resale houses, so older homes elsewhere often need a clear story on condition and price.

sections.h2: How do schools, transit and the weather affect a Wilsonville sale?
sections.html:
Three school districts touch the city. Most of Wilsonville is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District, whose Wilsonville schools include Wilsonville High School (opened 1995), Inza R. Wood and Meridian Creek middle schools, and Boeckman Creek, Boones Ferry and Lowrie primary schools. Charbonneau is in Canby, and areas to the west are in Sherwood.

Transit is unusual. The city withdrew from TriMet and created South Metro Area Regional Transit in 1988, and SMART offers free rides within city limits. The WES commuter rail, which began in February 2009, ends at Wilsonville Station.

The climate is marine west coast. Average annual precipitation is 42.62 inches, with December the wettest month at 6.67 inches. July and August highs average 87 degrees. The record high of 116 degrees came on June 28, 2021, and the record low of minus 15 came on December 23, 1998. Heat and freeze extremes put stress on roofs, cooling systems and pipes, which inspectors tend to check.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Wilsonville house?
sections.html:
Wilsonville owners in Clackamas County follow that county’s schedule, and owners in the Washington County section follow Washington County’s. Clackamas County’s current dates are November 16, 2026, February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027, with a 3% discount for full payment and 2% for two-thirds by the first date. Value appeals to the Property Value Appeals Board are due by December 31, 2026.

Washington County’s 2025 to 2026 statements used November 17, February 17 and May 15 as the three dates, with the same 3% and 2% discounts, and appeals ran through December 31, 2025.

The city also has urban renewal activity. Its Town Center covers more than 100 acres around Wilsonville Road and Town Center Loop, and any new urban renewal district needs voter approval under Measure 3-632. The city says it budgeted $64.4 million for operations in 2025 to 2026 and $51.6 million for capital projects, including the Boeckman Creek Interceptor.

sections.h2: What disclosure and closing rules apply to a Wilsonville seller?
sections.html:
Oregon requires a signed seller’s property disclosure statement for homes with up to four dwelling units, and the buyer gets five business days after delivery to revoke. That is set out in ORS 105.465 and 105.475.

ORS 105.470 excludes several sellers, such as lenders selling after foreclosure and court-appointed receivers, personal representatives and trustees. If your Wilsonville property is held in a trust or an estate, the exclusion may apply, and the title company can confirm. Keep records of repairs and permits, because a buyer who sees gaps may ask for time or a lower price.

sections.h2: How can a Wilsonville owner compare a cash sale with a listing?
sections.html:
A cash sale avoids showings, buyer financing and appraisal contingencies, and the buyer takes the property in its current condition. For a landlord, it can also mean selling with fewer move-out and cleaning steps.

Ask for a written offer and a closing statement, and compare it with a listing estimate after repairs, commission, tax proration, carrying costs and expected days on market. If the property sits in the Washington County section, ask the title officer which county rules apply.

faqs.q: Is Wilsonville in Clackamas County or Washington County?
faqs.a: Wilsonville is mostly in Clackamas County, with its northern section in Washington County. Your tax statement shows which county bills your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Wilsonville?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied homes is $615,300. It is a citywide survey figure, not an appraisal of any house.

faqs.q: What share of Wilsonville homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figure is 49.0%, so about half of occupied homes are rented.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Wilsonville house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. Charbonneau is in the Canby School District, and areas to the west are in the Sherwood School District.

faqs.q: When are Wilsonville property taxes due?
faqs.a: For Clackamas County parcels, the current dates are November 16, 2026, February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027. Washington County parcels follow that county's separate November, February and May dates.
Charbonneau is a planned golf course community south of the Willamette River that the city annexed in 1971. It has about 3,500 residents and is served by Canby schools.
